inspection.method: Opened each finished PNG through view_image detail original; all three displayed at native 1536x1024. Opened seven eligible originals, rendered model and both drawn staging files. Original photographs displayed with tool downsampling; source files remain unchanged.

findings: Neet has four distinguishable fine legs with grounded paws, a continuous full narrow torso, projecting muzzle, large triangular ears and a tiny nub. His three-quarter rear view agrees with N19 rather than the generated model texture.

Buddy lies in one continuous neck-ribcage-pelvis shape; chin rests on paired forepaws and bent hindquarters meet the rug. B19 supports the chin-down face and B29 supports the elongated trunk. Face/ear furnishings remain regional; torso is close and smooth.

Warm bathroom aperture frames both humans with brushing gestures while alert Neet watches and Buddy rests apart. Human faces remain provisional. Door/floor/rug perspective and cast contact are coherent; no detached limb or inappropriate prop is visible. Narrow opening and low viewpoint communicate surveillance against sleepy indifference.

Neet stands with four grounded connected limbs, full torso, a visible nub and broad triangular ears. Smooth fawn surface has no engraved curls or shag silhouette. His lowered open mouth faces the distinct fallen green leaf, making the disproportionate warning readable.

Buddy has paired bent forelegs rooted at the shoulder and two differently flexed hindlegs rooted at the pelvis. Continuous dark belly and neck connect the raised head to the supported recline; lower back/hip contact anchors him to mulch. B05 supports bent pale forepaws and ventral coloring, while B29 supplies body continuity rather than exact supine measurements.

Light muzzle, curved brows and ear fringe identify Buddy without spreading shag across the body. His belly-up glance is complementary to Neet’s stance. Fence, bench, ground scale and shared light read consistently; final warning precedes the subsequent leaf-on-shoulder incident, as required.

Neet’s seated pelvis, grounded foreleg and raised glass-contact foreleg are connected and supported; tiny nub and smooth short coat remain visible. Buddy sits with a continuous back, visible neck, substantial grounded forelegs and folded haunches; no limb ownership or support defect identified.

Glass separates the dogs from the two seated diners, candle, bowls and naan. Neet’s raised paw contrasts with Buddy’s purposeful table-facing wait, correctly depicting the pre-sheera-return protest. Indoor/outdoor scale, furniture perspective and human continuity are coherent; likeness of humans remains provisional.

Resolved: Buddy outer nape and neck now form a close continuous charcoal contour into shoulder; pointed ruff removed. Throat below beard also shortened into the chest. Furnished ear, pale beard, eyebrows and distal paws remain regional and distinguishable. The result agrees with the previously opened B04/B06/B29 close coat evidence.

Whole replacement checked: smooth torso remains free of engraved curls; neck/head, spine, haunches and four-limb seated construction remain connected. Neet retains supported seated pelvis, grounded foreleg, raised glass-contact paw, triangular ears and tiny nub. Diners, food, candle, glass, room and floor contacts retain scene continuity. No material regression found.

MATERIAL GROOMING DEFECT: pointed long tufts run from Buddy’s nape down the outer neck into the shoulder (approximately x1115–1210,y295–465), with additional long spikes on the throat/chest boundary (approximately x1035–1075,y408–555). These change the silhouette into a shaggy neck ruff despite the smooth flank. B04/B06 show close neck/chest fields beneath localized muzzle/ear furnishings; B29 shows a close outer neck/back. This is drawn fur length, not subtle watercolor grain. Remove that raised neck/shoulder/throat fringe while preserving documented ear, brow, muzzle and paw furnishings. Reinspect the entire actual replacement; do not infer clearance from the edit prompt.
